questions.text: Let G be a group of 35 elements. Then the largest possible size of a subgroup of G other than G itself is _______.
questions.solution:
By Lagrange's theorem, the order of a subgroup divides the order of the group. Divisors of 35: 1, 5, 7, 35.

Excluding G itself, the largest possible is 7 (a group of order 35 is cyclic and has subgroups of every divisor order).

Answer: 7

questions.text: Let [latex]R[/latex] be the set of all binary relations on the set {1,2,3}. Suppose a relation is chosen from [latex]R[/latex] at random. The probability that the chosen relation is reflexive (round off to 3 decimal places) is ______.
questions.solution:
A relation on a 3-element set is any subset of the [latex]3\times3=9[/latex] pairs [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^9[/latex] relations.
Reflexive: the 3 pairs (a, a) must be included; the other 6 are free [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^6[/latex].

[latex]P=\frac{2^6}{2^9}=\frac18=0.125[/latex]

Answer: 0.125

questions.text: Suppose Y is distributed uniformly in the open interval (1,6). The probability that the polynomial [latex]3x^2+6xY+3Y+6[/latex] has only real roots is (rounded off to 1 decimal place) _________.
questions.solution:
Real roots need discriminant [latex]\ge0[/latex]:
[latex](6Y)^2-4\cdot3\cdot(3Y+6)\ge0\Rightarrow36Y^2-36Y-72\ge0\Rightarrow(Y-2)(Y+1)\ge0[/latex]

For Y in (1, 6) this means [latex]Y\ge2[/latex]. Probability [latex]=\frac{6-2}{6-1}=\frac45=0.8[/latex]

Answer: 0.8

questions.text:
Consider the first order predicate formula:
[latex]\forall x[\forall z\; z|x\Rightarrow ((z=x)\vee (z=1))\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\exists w(w> x)\wedge (\forall z \; z|w\Rightarrow ((w=z)\vee (z=1)))][/latex]
Here 'a|b' denotes that 'a divides b', where a and b are integers. Consider the following sets:

S1: {1, 2, 3, ..., 100}
S2: Set of all positive integers
S3: Set of all integers
Which of the above sets satisfy [latex]\varphi[/latex] ?
questions.solution:
The formula says: for every x that is prime (only divisors are 1 and x), there is a larger prime w. In other words, there is no largest prime.

- S1 = {1, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 100}: 97 is prime, but no prime larger than 97 is in S1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fails.
- S2, S3: there are infinitely many primes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] satisfied.

Answer: S2 and S3

questions.text: Two numbers are chosen independently and uniformly at random from the set {1, 2, ..., 13}. The probability (rounded off to 3 decimal places) that their 4-bit (unsigned) binary representations have the same most significant bit is ___________
questions.solution:
In 4 bits, the MSB is 1 for 8-13 (6 numbers) and 0 for 1-7 (7 numbers).

[latex]P=\left(\frac{7}{13}\right)^2+\left(\frac{6}{13}\right)^2=\frac{49+36}{169}=\frac{85}{169}\approx0.503[/latex]

Answer: 0.503
